title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, carried over from p.32: X/S is a relative smooth curve. 𝒫 is a complete augmented O_X-algebra with augmentation ideal J, J/J² = Ω an invertible O_X-module, so locally 𝒫 ≅ Ô_X[[z]]. A connection C : 𝒫 → 𝒫 ⊗̂ Ω¹_{X/S} is a derivation over d on O_X. Writing C|_Ω = (ω_i) in ∏ Sym^i(Ω) ⊗ Ω¹, one has C(J^i) ⊂ J^{i−1} ⊗̂ Ω¹. The degree-lowering symbol gr^i → gr^{i−1} ⊗ Ω¹ is then O-linear and given by ϖ₀.

This page:
(1) ϖ₀ ∈ Γ(Ω^{-1} ⊗ Ω¹_{X/S}) = Hom(Ω, Ω¹_{X/S}) does not depend on the choice of local splitting. It is the 'symplectic / Hamiltonian' homomorphism; Grothendieck first wrote 'Ham' and crossed it out. In foliation terms it is the Kodaira–Spencer-type map measuring how the horizontal foliation moves the section.
(2) Definition: C is 'régulière' when ϖ₀ : Ω ≅ Ω¹_{X/S} is an isomorphism. Geometrically, the horizontal foliation is everywhere transversal to the zero section. This is exactly Gunning's / Beilinson–Drinfeld's oper (indigenous bundle) transversality condition.
(3) Proposition. Let 0 → Ω → E → O_X → 0 be exact. Let P = ℙ(E) be the corresponding P¹-bundle over X with section σ, and Ŝ = O_{P̂} the formal completion of P along σ. This is an augmented algebra of the above type with J/J² = Ω.
- Conn(P) denotes the (projective, i.e. PGL₂-) connections on P. Each induces a connection ĉ on Ŝ, giving a map Conn(P) → Conn(Ŝ).
- Conn*(Ŝ) is the set of regular connections on Ŝ, and Conn*(P) is its inverse image in Conn(P).
- G (resp. G₀) is the group of augmented automorphisms of Ŝ that are the identity mod J³ (resp. J⁴). Grothendieck writes 'mod m³ (J⁴)'; probably J³ is meant for G.
- Claim: (c, g) ↦ g·ĉ gives a bijection Conn*(P) × G₀ → Conn*(Ŝ).
- In words: every regular formal connection along the section is uniquely, up to formal automorphisms tangent to the identity to order 3, the completion of a genuine projective (Riccati-type) connection on the P¹-bundle.
- This is the formal counterpart of the fact that a projective (Möbius) coordinate is determined by its 2-jet. The stabiliser of a point in PGL₂ maps isomorphically onto 2-jets of coordinate changes.
(4) Corollary. For c ∈ Conn*(P), St(c) = {g ∈ G : g·ĉ ∈ Im Conn*(P)} maps bijectively onto G/G₀.
- G/G₀ ≅ Hom(Ω, Ω^{⊗3}) = Γ(X, Ω^{⊗2}) via the z³-coefficient.
- Through ϖ₀ this is Γ(X, (Ω¹_{X/S})^{⊗2}): the quadratic differentials.
- So the regular projective connections (projective structures / opers) on a fixed underlying formal object form a torsor under quadratic differentials. This is the Schwarzian-derivative picture.
- The margin adds that the stabiliser G_c of c in Conn*(Ŝ) reduces to the identity.

Purpose: an algebraic, relative (over a base S), formal-geometric foundation of projective structures and uniformization on curves.
errors: The exponents are inconsistent: 'mod m³ (J⁴)'. For the corollary G/G₀ ≅ quadratic differentials, G must be the identity mod J³ and G₀ the identity mod J⁴; the 'm³' is probably a slip.
'est bijective (resp. bijective)' is unclear. The intended 'resp.' statement for G (perhaps surjectivity, or a statement on stabilisers) is not stated.

Characteristic hypotheses are missing. The normalisation by automorphisms mod J⁴ and the Schwarzian identification need 2 and 3 invertible on S (cf. Mochizuki's and Hoshi's char-p treatments). Nothing on the page restricts the characteristic.
No proof is given; the page ends the dossier with the corollary unfinished ('Ω^{⊗?}').

ideas.what: Symbol ϖ₀ : Ω → Ω¹_{X/S} of a connection on the formal completion along a section; 'regular' iff it is an isomorphism (horizontal foliation transversal to the section)
ideas.modern_name: oper / indigenous bundle transversality (Griffiths transversality condition for PGL₂-opers)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning (1967, indigenous bundles); Beilinson–Drinfeld (opers, 1990s); Mochizuki (1996, p-adic Teichmüller)

ideas.what: Regular formal connections along the section = completions of projective connections × automorphisms ≡ id mod J⁴ (unique normal form)
ideas.modern_name: formal normal form / 'formal opers' via jets of coordinates modulo PGL₂ (Aut O-torsor description)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Beilinson–Drinfeld; Frenkel–Ben-Zvi (vertex algebras and algebraic curves); classical Schwarzian theory

ideas.what: Projective structures form a torsor under Γ(X, (Ω¹)^{⊗2}), obtained as G/G₀ (3-jet coefficient of formal automorphisms)
ideas.modern_name: Schwarzian derivative; affine space of projective structures over quadratic differentials

missed.claim: A relative (over arbitrary S), purely formal-algebraic treatment of projective connections. It works on the completed P¹-bundle along a section, with an intrinsic 'regularity' (oper-transversality) invariant ϖ₀ ∈ Hom(Ω, Ω¹_{X/S}) and a unique normal-form decomposition Conn*(Ŝ) = Conn*(P) × G₀. Grothendieck's version anticipates the oper / Aut(O)-torsor formalism of Beilinson–Drinfeld and Frenkel–Ben-Zvi and the indigenous-bundle formalism of Mochizuki, if the notes predate them (undated).
missed.quote: On dit que c est connexion régulière si la section ϖ₀ de Ω^{-1}⊗Ω¹_{X/S} est inversible
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents Grothendieck working on opers and uniformization in a relative scheme-theoretic setting. Specialists would know the mathematics, but not that Grothendieck formulated it this way.

missed.claim: The characterisation of regular formal connections as 'projectives' and the stabiliser statements (resp. for G, triviality of G_c) are left unproved. The base-change / characteristic-p behaviour, relevant to Mochizuki-type theory, is not addressed.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mild: the relative formal normal form over general S, including small characteristics, is a natural statement but is covered in spirit by later work.

deep.surprise_reason: The content (opers, Schwarzian torsor of projective structures under quadratic differentials) is classical or later well established. The interesting point is Grothendieck's intrinsic formal-completion formulation with the regularity symbol ϖ₀ and a normal-form proposition over a general base. It is unpublished and anticipates the oper formalism, but would not shock a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'Ŝ = O_{P̂}' is the formal completion of P along the section σ (P̂ = completion), not a hat on p.
'mod m³ (J⁴)' likely means G = id mod J³ and G₀ = id mod J⁴ (read 'G (G₀) ... mod J³ (J⁴)').
'{+(i.e. projectives [?])+}' is a plausible reading but uncertain.
Corollary target 'Γ(X, Ω^{⊗?})' should probably be read Γ(X, Ω^{⊗2}) (quadratic differentials via ϖ₀); the written exponent is illegible.
'[-Ham-]' was crossed out, presumably 'Hamiltonien', next to 'symplectique'.
